papers.title: BALMS: Benchmarking Agentic LLMs for Longitudinal Mental Health Sensing
papers.authors: Wu, Pillai, Chen, Zhang, Regmi, Campbell et al. (Dartmouth)
papers.what: Measures whether an LLM agent can read months of wearable signal and predict a self-report wellbeing score with a grounded rationale, across 3 longitudinal datasets, 2 task families, 3 agentic paradigms and 5 backbones, and finds that zero-shot agents rarely beat a per-subject mean baseline except with the strongest backbones or with compact semantic features.
papers.builds_on: GLOBEM (Xu 2023, ICD9EG8Q); LLMs are Few-Shot Health Learners (Liu 2023, JX3X3KH5); HEARTS (2026, 2603.06638); MindScape (Nepal 2024, K4PR34NU)

papers.title: Cliff: Learning Process Rewards from the First Mistake
papers.authors: Han, Wang, Ramaneti, Hao, Friedland, Kong
papers.what: Uses an off-the-shelf LLM to mark the first reasoning error in each rollout, splits the trace at that index into a correct prefix and an incorrect suffix, and turns the split into token-level advantages, beating on-policy distillation by 15 percent and GRPO by 7 percent across 12 scenarios even with weak teachers.
papers.builds_on: DeepSeek-R1 (2025, Z5IWHZAE); Chain-of-Thought Prompting (Wei 2023, HBLPTRMY); Does On-Policy Distillation Really Distill? (2026, 2608.31046)

papers.title: Aspire: Can Models Self-Evolve from Vague Goals?
papers.authors: Wu, Zhang, Shi, Lei, Zhou et al. (ByteDance Seed)
papers.what: Gives an agent only a natural-language capability goal with the evaluation tasks hidden, so it must choose data, update method and stopping rule itself, and finds across 520 expert-authored items in six goals that weight-level gains are sparse and unstable, the best evolved harness stays below the engineered Qwen-Agent reference, and continued search can erase earlier gains.
papers.builds_on: Memory Mechanisms Survey (Huang 2026, BDY3HUCV); Agent AI Survey (Durante 2024, Z9WZPMNU); Repo-To-Skill (2026, 2609.02749)

papers.title: CRISP: Cliff-awaRe Input-adaptive Sparse Prefilling with Structural-Mass-Motivated Routing
papers.authors: Nguyen, Nguyen, Dernoncourt, Rossi, Chen, Nguyen
papers.what: Replaces divergence-based sparse-attention routing with a structural mass measure read straight off the proxy attention map, and shows that cumulative coverage thresholds admit O(n) background noise at long context, so a sink-aware threshold recovers up to 28.0 percentage points on retrieval tasks while reaching a 5.30x attention speedup at 512k tokens.
papers.builds_on: Attention Is All You Need (Vaswani 2017, PHB9VRVM); Declarative Attention (2026, 2609.02737); DeepSeek-V3 (2024, 2JCKA7GI)
